releases.displayName: Demo Update & A Big Thank You!

items.text: We wanted to start off by saying a big thank you to everyone who played the demo this last week! Next Fest has just finished and Steam has told us that we managed to make it into the top 50 most played demos which we couldn’t have achieved without your support and enthusiasm, it really means a lot!
We’ve also been reading all of your feedback in the forums and have been adding your comments and suggestions to our backlog so that we continually improve the game after we launch tomorrow.

To show our appreciation we’ve decided to extend the availability of our demo until 3rd July 2024. We’ll also be rolling out a new demo update tomorrow morning that will contain a number of fixes chief amongst these being:
More keybinding options including rotate building and space bar pause
The game no longer gets stuck when the player presses the Esc button just after confirming the change settings in 'Autosave Interval'
Autosave timer now works after selecting ‘YES’ on warning
Save data no longer corrupts when saving on a full disk
Middle mouse button can now be used to scroll back in from the tactical map
Camera rotation sensitivity has been lowered when using the middle mouse button
Zoom in and out controls are now smoother
You can now interact with the notifications bar while viewing the tactical map
You can now switch between the upgrade and downgrade tools simultaneously in the radial menu
Improved performance and optimisation
Various visual and UI fixes
Various audio fixes
Various localisation fixes
Various achievements fixes
Various controller and input fixes

Most importantly this new demo will also allow players to continue their saves if they choose to purchase the full game. It is important to note however that players who installed the demo BEFORE 11am CEST on 19th June 2024 will need to start a new save as the update will wipe existing saves (apologies for the inconvenience but this is the only way that we can get the demo saves to correctly carry through into the main game!)
Crazy Goat Games & PQube

After having focussed our attention on shipbuilding, fleet management, and diplomacy in our last few updates, we’re now going to dive into the different gameplay modes you’ll be able to experience at launch.

There are two modes of play in Republic of Pirates – campaign mode and freeplay mode, and today, we will teach you all about the differences between these modes, shine the spotlight on a couple of our freeplay maps and show you how progression works outside of campaign mode!

notes.title: New Horizons: Campaign and Freeplay Mode

items.text: Looking for a more story-driven experience? Embark on an epic adventure in campaign mode and rebuild the once glorious Republic of Pirates. Your rag-tag crew of misfits will offer advice in the form of tutorials which will aid you in progressing your story further. Follow the main missions and quest objectives to find out where your journey will lead you!
Begin your adventure on the Forgotten Archipelago map and choose from three difficulties to customise your experience to your liking!
Play in freeplay mode for a more casual and open-ended experience. You will get the option to pick from two additional maps with unique geography and layouts.

In freeplay mode, there are no main missions to complete, and gameplay will not be tutorialised. Instead, you will simply work to grow your population and your republic while conquering the whole archipelago.
How you play is ultimately up to you.

notes.title: Cementing Your Legacy: Progression in Freeplay Mode

items.text: Despite giving you a pressure-free gaming experience, you’ll still have the opportunity to progress in freeplay mode. Contrary to the quest objectives you receive in campaign mode, your crew of misfits will no longer offer you main missions in freeplay mode. Instead, you’ll progress through the map by hitting population milestones. Once you have reached a specific milestone, you will unlock a new set of buildings which will ultimately allow you to develop your city further, and move onto the next population milestone and so on!
Until next time!
Crazy Goat Games & PQube
In our last few posts, we’ve given a detailed breakdown of how to manage your fleet, conquer the archipelago, and cultivate your relationships with other factions.

Today, we’re excited to be revealing a new combat mechanic in the form of active ship skills. This recently implemented system will add an extra layer of strategy to naval battles and will make fleet building and composition even more impactful!
In update 4 we looked at the role of the fleet, shipbuilding materials, ship classes, and customisation.

To recap, you will use your fleet to explore the archipelago, and attack merchants and rival pirate ships. In doing so, you will receive valuable loot which will help you to build more advanced ships and conquer additional islands. By conquering more islands you’ll then gain access to rare resources and more land to expand your republic.

Remember that every ship class has its own unique stat line, but with the addition of the new active skills, you’ll need to be increasingly mindful of the importance of fleet composition and combat tactics when planning your next raid!

notes.title: Man the Cannons: An Introduction to Active Skills

items.text: Depending on its class, each ship now has access to one of five active skills. These skills can be triggered during combat by clicking on the ship and selecting the active skill button in the ship unit UI. It's worth noting that if several ships have been group selected, you will also be able to see all their active skills at once and can easily choose the order in which they trigger, depending on your current needs.

notes.title: Active skills can be divided into three broad categories

items.text: Offensive: Skills that directly attack and damage enemy units
Disruptive: Skills that debuff enemy units in various ways
Support: Skills that buff allied ships

Once you have used an active skill, there will be a short cooldown period before you will be able to use it again. Cooldown times vary depending on the skill and the ship’s class, so make sure to plan your attacks carefully.
See below for a full breakdown of the five skills.
Skill description: Fires a scattershot in a cone. It will hit all ships within the cone which can be rotated 360 degrees around the centre of the ship. The scattershot deals light damage.
Skill type: Offensive
Buildable ship class with skill: Cog, Brigantine
Skill description: Fires a smoke bomb to a target location within range. This will create a small area of effect upon landing causing all enemy attacks from affected ships to miss for a short period.
Skill type: Disruptive
Buildable ship class with skill: Ketch, Galleon
Skill description: Gives all nearby ships a temporary boost to their speed stat allowing them to traverse the map faster or escape from a difficult battle.
Skill type: Support
Buildable ship classes with skill: Frigate
Skill description: Attack an enemy ship within range and damage their sails to slow them down for a limited time.
Skill type: Disruptive
Buildable ship classes with skill: Brig
Skill description: Unleashes a devastating attack on an individual enemy unit within range. Your unit will attack several times, inflicting massive damage on your enemy in a short period of time.
Skill type: Offensive
Buildable ship classes with skill: Barque, Man-of-War
Until next time!
